standard_prerequisites.name: The non-dependent recursor of Lemma 6.12.5
standard_prerequisites.statement: From c : prd a:A C a -> Q and p : prd b:B prd y:C(f b) (c(f b,y) = c(g b, D b y)) one gets k : (Sigma w:W P(w)) -> Q with k(c-tilde'(a,x)) := c(a,x).
standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma is stated in exactly that situation and its goal is the second computation rule for this k.

standard_prerequisites.name: Computation of ap on pair paths for componentwise maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: If k(x,y) := d(x)(y) then ap k (pairpath(s,r)) equals the displayed composite, provided full transport coherence is included; the statement is the author's auxiliary lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at source lines 1993-1994 with the four instantiations at lines 1995-1999 to reduce the goal.

standard_prerequisites.name: Computation rule of the induction principle for W
standard_prerequisites.statement: apd d (p(b)) is the composite of equation (6.12.6), passed across the equivalence of thm:dpath-arrow.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the second factor at source lines 2005-2006 computable.

core_obligations: Recall that p-tilde'(b,y) := pairpath(p(b), q) with q : trans (p b) y = D b y from thm:transport-is-given, so that ap k (p-tilde'(b,y)) can be computed by the author's auxiliary lemma (source lines 1993-1994).
Instantiate that lemma at x_1 := c(f b), x_2 := c(g b), y_1 := y, y_2 := D b y, s := p(b) and r := q (source lines 1995-1999).
Compute the first factor ap d(x_2)(r) using that d(c(a),x) := c(a,x), giving ap (c(g b, -))(q) (source lines 2003-2004).

Compute the second factor by the induction computation rule for W, which identifies apd d (p b) with the composite of equation (6.12.6) passed across thm:dpath-arrow, and rewrite it along the displayed three-step chain at lines 2007-2019.
Substitute both values into the auxiliary lemma and cancel the paths in pairs, leaving p(b,y) (source line 2020).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the goal with the auxiliary pair-path computation lemma and list the instantiation.
Identify the two factors the auxiliary lemma requires: the ap of the fixed second variable and the applicative form of apd d (p b).
Compute the second factor along the chain of transports and trivial transports.
Substitute and cancel, leaving the hypothesis p(b,y).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.12.8 at source lines 1989-1991: in the situation of the non-dependent recursion principle of Lemma 6.12.5, ap k (p-tilde'(b,y)) = p(b,y). The proof (source lines 1992-2021) is the last and most technical step of the flattening lemma and is not a computation: the pair path p-tilde'(b,y) has to be expanded into pairpath(p(b),q) using the canonical transport (line 1993), the auxiliary pair-path lemma must be instantiated at six named arguments (lines 1995-1999), its two factors then have to be computed separately, the first from the definition of the curried function d (lines 2003-2004) and the second from the induction computation rule for W passed across thm:dpath-arrow (lines 2005-2006), and the final identification is the observation that all paths in the resulting chain cancel in pairs (line 2020).
